answer: Each agent must root a single yarrow plant on a narrow private computational ledge that only produces a unique pearl after continuous 72-hour growth simulation with real-time environmental noise. The pearl's concentric rings embed a one-time nonce only the controlling process can generate. A Sybil attacker must run an independent full simulation for every clone identity; the ledge binds the process to one core and the pearl fails verification if growth is paused or shared, forcing the attacker to pay full energy and memory cost per identity with no multiplexing.
